title: Airport Distance Calculator: Great-Circle Miles
description: Compare any two airports with the Airport Distance Calculator: great-circle distance in km and miles plus a rough airborne-time reference. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, New York JFK to Los Angeles LAX measures approx. 3,974 km (2,470 miles) on the great circle — the shortest surface path between the two runways' cities, before airways and weather add their share.
quick_answer: The Airport Distance Calculator compares two airports by the shortest path between them — the great-circle distance — and reports it in kilometres and miles with a rough airborne-time reference. Search by airport name or code, and treat the result as the geographic baseline every flight route is longer than.
steps_intro: Two airports, one baseline number — the figure airlines, mileage programs and route planners all start from:

body.t: Award charts and mileage runs are priced on distance. Checking the great-circle figure between two airports tells you what a ticket should earn before you trust a booking page's estimate.
Before asking whether a non-stop exists — the
answers that — the distance tells you whether the hop is a regional shuttle or a long-haul commitment for crew, aircraft and fuel.

Cities with several airports (New York, London, Paris) reward a distance check: the nearer airport to your meeting is not always the one with the shorter flight. Run both pairs and compare totals, not just air time.
Airport pairs make great-circle geometry concrete — the numbers are real, the airports are findable on any map, and the curved route surprises every class the first time.

JFK to LAX: approx. 3,974.3 km (2,469.5 mi), initial bearing 273.8° — almost due west, bending north as the route progresses. Chicago O'Hare to Dallas/Fort Worth is a shorter domestic hop: approx. 1,290.0 km (801.6 mi).

London Heathrow to Paris Charles de Gaulle is only approx. 347.0 km (215.6 mi) — a distance many travellers drive — while Heathrow to Frankfurt stretches to approx. 653.5 km (406.1 mi). Short European sectors are where airport choice changes the trip most.

faq: Why is the flown distance longer than this figure?

Aircraft follow airways, departure and arrival procedures, and weather-avoidance paths — none of which is the geometric minimum. This calculator reports the baseline great-circle distance; an airline's published mileage for the same pair is normally a few percent higher.
Can I enter IATA codes directly?
Yes — search accepts airport names and three-letter codes such as JFK, LAX or LHR. If two airports share a name fragment, pick from the matched list so the coordinates are the right ones.
What does the airborne-time reference assume?
A simple cruise-speed reference for scale only. It ignores climb, descent, taxi and winds, so use it to compare pairs — never to plan a connection.

The search covers the airport dataset the site ships, which favours airports with scheduled service and published coordinates. A private strip without a listing can still be measured by entering its coordinates in a point-to-point tool.
Is the distance measured runway to runway?

It is measured between the airports' published reference coordinates — effectively airport centre to airport centre. For city-scale planning that is the meaningful figure; runway thresholds differ by a kilometre or two at large fields.
Can I find the midpoint between two airports?
Yes — the Airport Midpoint by Coordinates tool applies the same spherical geometry and returns the halfway point of the pair.
Why does the bearing from A to B not simply reverse?

On a sphere the return initial bearing is not the outward bearing plus 180°, because the great circle is followed in the opposite direction from a different starting geometry. JFK to LAX starts at 273.8°; LAX to JFK starts at 65.9°, not 93.8°.
